<h1 id="how-to-write-shop-files-with-ai" data-toc-id="how-to-write-shop-files-with-ai">How to Write Shop Files with AI</h1>
<p></p>
<p>
  Quite a few people have this thought: creating items in the editor is indeed simple, but when the volume gets large it is still a grind, so they wonder whether AI could be used to write the shop files. For this, since v1.1.8 the mod supports exporting the shop's information from the editor as JSON to the clipboard, or importing JSON from the clipboard back into the editor. Note that this exists only to turn the information into the more familiar JSON format so it is easier for AI and for you to read; it does not mean the shop's final saved format is JSON.
</p>
<h2 id="how-to-export-and-import-json-information" data-toc-id="how-to-export-and-import-json-information">How to Export and Import JSON Information</h2>
<p>
  After you create a project in the editor, two options appear under File: "Export data to clipboard" and "Import data from clipboard". They do exactly what their names suggest: the shop's information is converted to JSON on the clipboard for convenient editing, and once you are done editing you simply import it back.
</p><img
  src="data:image/png;base64,"
  alt="">
<div type="warning" data-type="admonition" data-admo-type="warning">
  <div data-type="admonition-title">Friendly Reminder</div>
  <div data-type="admonition-content">
    <p>
      If you import data into the editor and everything in the shop preview seems unchanged, do not doubt yourself first: after re-importing you have not selected a category, so the shop still shows the previously cached information. At this point, simply select a category again.
    </p>
  </div>
</div>
<h2 id="how-to-feed-the-shop-information-structure-to-ai" data-toc-id="how-to-feed-the-shop-information-structure-to-ai">How to Feed the Shop Information Structure to AI</h2>
<p>The most rigorous approach is of course to feed the mod's source code to the AI. After all, this data is updated in real time, and any structure I provide here could change in the future, so instead I am providing the project's source code paths and examples.</p>
<p>Source code for the shop information project:</p>
<p>Shop: <a
    href="https://github.com/zhenshiz/ViScriptShop/blob/master/src/main/java/com/viscriptshop/gui/data/ShopInfo.java"
    target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer nofollow">Shop information</a></p>
<p>Category: <a
    href="https://github.com/zhenshiz/ViScriptShop/blob/master/src/main/java/com/viscriptshop/gui/data/CategoryInfo.java"
    target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer nofollow">Category information</a></p>
<p>Item: <a
    href="https://github.com/zhenshiz/ViScriptShop/blob/master/src/main/java/com/viscriptshop/gui/data/MerchantInfo.java"
    target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer nofollow">Item information</a> <a
    href="https://github.com/zhenshiz/ViScriptShop/blob/master/src/main/java/com/viscriptshop/gui/data/ItemMatchRule.java"
    target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer nofollow">Trade item matching rules (item component matching)</a> <a
    href="https://github.com/zhenshiz/ViScriptShop/blob/master/src/main/java/com/viscriptshop/gui/data/MerchantFlagGroup.java"
    target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer nofollow">Phase conditions</a></p>
<p>Alternatively, you can write out the complete data structure yourself and feed it to the AI to let it judge on its own. This is a bit more convenient, but it certainly will not be as accurate as feeding the source code directly.</p>
